sample_unit: AI scribe tools (notes rated by 30 blinded raters across 5 standardized cases, compared with 18 human note takers)

links.outcome: Ambient scribe note quality (modified PDQI-9) versus human-produced notes, blinded raters
links.effect: Human notes scored higher than AI in all 5 cases; low back pain case human 43.8 vs AI 20.3, difference -23.5 (CI -29.2 to -17.9); AI lower in all 10 domains.
links.quote: Notes generated by AI had lower-quality scores than human-generated notes across 5 standardized care cases.

links.outcome: AI scribe note quality across domains including thoroughness, organization, and usefulness
links.effect: Pooled domain analysis showed lower AI scores across all 10 domains, largest deficits: thorough -1.23, organized -1.06, useful -1.03.
links.quote: Pooled domain analysis showed lower AI scores across all 10 domains, with the largest deficits in domains related to being thorough (-1.23 [CI, -1.82 to -0.65]), organized (-1.06 [CI, -1.65 to -0.47]), and useful (-1.03 [CI, -1.61 to -0.44]).

links.outcome: Variation in note quality across competing vendor AI scribe products
links.effect: 11 vendor AI scribe tools were compared side by side on standardized cases; all scored below human notes, with wide CIs (e.g., AI 20.3 [15.4 to 25.2] in back pain case).
links.quote: Prior evaluations have been vendor specific and not focused on measures of documentation quality.

unlisted_practices: Independent vendor-neutral evaluation of ambient scribe note quality using standardized patient cases and blinded raters

screen.reason: Empirical study comparing the note quality of 11 ambient AI scribes against human-written notes on simulated standardized clinical cases using the modified PDQI-9 instrument.
